cohort: The study included 120 children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders (ASD or ADHD) and 120 control participants from the National Center for Autism/Medical City Complex in Baghdad.
finding: Five perinatal factors – low birth weight, newborn complications, preterm-birth, being the last child, and caesarean section delivery – were significantly associated with child behavioral disorders.
mod_finding: Delivery via a caesarean section was identified as a significant perinatal factor associated with child behavioral disorders.
cross-section timing: The study data was collected from January to April 2022, examining past neonatal events and current psychotropic medication use in children and adolescents.
birth_weight: N/A (Low birth weight was an exposure, but specific weights were not detailed)
gest_age: N/A (Preterm-birth was an exposure, but specific gestational ages were not detailed)
